clue.text: Hike, having plan to cross Britain and run back

indicators.note: the plan is made to cross, i.e. stretch over, the other letters, so it holds them inside

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area

indicators.note: back says the pair of pieces Britain and run are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, stands for Britain
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A walker plans a route across Britain and back again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hike' looks like a walk, matching the surface's trek across Britain, but it is a price rise; 'back' and 'to cross' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: A price rise, an increase added to cost, is commonly called a hike.

clue.text: Like an eagle one spotted following endless water course

indicators.note: following places the remaining pieces after the shortened water
endless says the word for water loses its final letter

parts.note: aqua is Latin for water, familiar from words like aquarium
one is the Roman numeral I, and a small i is the letter with a dot or spot over it
a line is a course or route, as in a line of action

explanation.surface: Someone spots an eagle following the course of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one spotted' is a playful nod to the lower-case i with its dot; 'endless' trims the final letter and 'following' sets the rest after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things resembling an eagle, especially a hooked nose like its beak.

clue.text: Gift-wrapped pasta oddly in carrier bag

indicators.note: the gift is wrapped round other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a knack is a gift or talent

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the word pasta

explanation.surface: A present of pasta is wrapped up and carried home in a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gift-wrapped' reads as one word for a present, but it splits into the synonym and the containment indicator; 'oddly' picks letters one, three and five.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack carried on the back is a bag for carrying belongings.

clue.text: Very close friend supports non-amateur team

indicators.note: in a down clue, the friend supports the rest by sitting beneath it

parts.note: a pro, a professional, is the opposite of an amateur
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team
mate is British slang for a friend

explanation.surface: A close friend backs a professional sports team.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'supports' puts MATE at the bottom, under PRO + XI.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means nearest or immediately adjacent, so very close in place or time.

clue.text: Religious rebel worried, being tied to a stake

parts.note: a post is a stake driven into the ground
ate in the sense of troubled, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: A heretic is anxious because he is tied to a stake for burning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' is a verb in the past, meaning 'ate' (gnawed at), not the adjective it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who renounces a religious faith is a rebel against that religion.

clue.text: Lawman confiscated portion of ecstasy from wayward Tyrolean teenager

indicators.note: confiscated means a piece is taken away from the following words before they are rearranged
wayward means the remaining letters go astray into a new order

parts.note: E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy, a small portion of it

explanation.surface: A government law officer seizes a pill of ecstasy from a wayward Austrian teen.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E from TYROLEAN TEENAGER and rearrange the fifteen remaining letters. Tyrolean means from the Tyrol, an Alpine region.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief law officer advising the government is a senior lawman.

clue.text: Stand programme shown regularly on TV

parts.note: a soap opera is a television programme broadcast several times a week
the box is British slang for television

explanation.surface: A TV stand and a regularly scheduled programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like a verb but is a noun; in a down entry 'on' simply puts the programme above the television.
explanation.definitionFit: A box once used to stand on when addressing crowds, hence a platform for opinions.

clue.text: Cupid gives up first love to, get a drink

indicators.note: gives up means one letter is surrendered and another, introduced by to get, put in its place

parts.note: an amoretto is a cherub or Cupid figure in art
love is zero in tennis, O; first means the first O in the word

explanation.surface: Cupid abandons his first love to go and have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In AMORETTO the first O is replaced by A. The page prints 'love to. get', a stray dot.
explanation.definitionFit: An almond-flavoured Italian liqueur, a type of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Before court case, former spouse put demand for money

indicators.note: before places the former spouse ahead of the court case

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
an action is a lawsuit brought in court

explanation.surface: Ahead of a lawsuit, someone's ex makes a financial demand.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a forcible demand for payment, such as an extortionate levy.

clue.text: Railwaymen, as it were, in nippy car

parts.note: NUR, the National Union of Railwaymen; reading the answer as an instruction turns the three letters round to make NUR

explanation.surface: A group of railway workers are in a small car, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it were' signals a reverse clue: the answer, read as RUN 'about' (turned round), gives NUR, the old National Union of Railwaymen.
explanation.definitionFit: A small light car for short trips is a nippy, easy-to-drive vehicle.

clue.text: Guerrilla put to death a group of soldiers

parts.note: zap is slang for kill
TA, the Territorial Army, the British army reserve

explanation.surface: A guerrilla leader executes a squad of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Emiliano Zapata was a Mexican revolutionary who led guerrilla forces.

clue.text: Airman circles tree giving more dazzling display

indicators.note: the airman circles the tree, going all round it

parts.note: a flier is a pilot or airman
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A pilot loops round a tree in a showy aerial display.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of a word meaning showy or ostentatious, so more dazzling.

clue.text: Wretched crewman caught boarding plane

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, a member of a ship's crew

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the letter goes inside the plane

parts.note: a jet is a plane
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A miserable sailor is caught getting onto an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means miserable or pitiful, a synonym for wretched.

clue.text: Headgear sported by fellow taking the waters at Vichy

indicators.note: taking joins the fellow to the waters, placing them next

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
eaux is French for waters; Vichy is a French spa town

explanation.surface: A man wearing a hat takes the cure at the French spa of Vichy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sported by' joins the definition to the wordplay; 'at Vichy' signals French.
explanation.definitionFit: French plural for hats, so items of headgear.

clue.text: Garden ultimately this ugly, if allowed to grow wild?

definitions.text: Garden ultimately this ugly, if allowed to grow wild?

indicators.note: grow wild suggests letters running riot into a new order
ultimately takes the final letter of garden

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A neglected garden will become this hideous if left to run wild.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the last letter of Garden, plus THIS UGLY, rearranged; the whole clue also describes an overgrown garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue pictures an overgrown garden, which would be unpleasant to look at.

clue.text: Cards fell

definitions.meaning: a full pack of playing cards
to knock someone to the ground with a punch

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a pack of cards; the verb means to floor someone.

clue.text: Lawyer plays big part defending leader of disreputable scoundrels

parts.note: DA, district attorney, an American lawyer

indicators.note: the stars defend the letter by surrounding it

parts.note: an actor who stars plays a big part

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of disreputable

explanation.surface: A lawyer takes a leading role defending a disreputable villain.
explanation.walkthrough: DA (district attorney) is an American lawyer; 'defending' wraps the actor's word round the leader of disreputable.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned word for cowards or villains, so scoundrels.

clue.text: Secure a prisoner in jail? The opposite

indicators.note: in would put the prisoner inside the jail, but the next words reverse that
the opposite says the containment runs the other way, with the jail inside the prisoner

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Locking a prisoner in jail is a secure arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'a prisoner in jail' would put the prisoner inside; 'The opposite' flips it so a jail sits inside the convict, with the A joining the jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyphenated, it means unbreakable or watertight, as in a cast-iron alibi.

clue.text: Decorate golden handle with new paint, no trouble

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
handle is slang for a name

indicators.note: no means trouble is removed from the word paint

parts.note: pain means trouble or bother

explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes PAIN out of paint, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to adorn or embellish something.

clue.text: Means of getting to the top, say, for judges

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.words: Means of getting to the top
parts.note: ways up are routes for climbing to the summit

explanation.surface: Routes to the summit are examined by competition judges.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh something up is to assess or evaluate it, as a judge does.

clue.text: Growth a bit less than average

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in 'not a whit'
low means below average

explanation.surface: Something grows a little less than usual.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful swelling or infection near a fingernail, a kind of growth.

clue.text: Murphy's in poor condition reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals the word for shabby is heard rather than read

parts.note: tatty means shabby and worn

explanation.surface: Murphy is said to be in bad shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy is slang for a potato (from Irish associations); TATTIE is the Scottish word. 'Murphy's' is 'Murphy is', matching the answer with its link 's.

clue.text: By agreement, hot drink's circulated as late evening beverage

indicators.note: circulated means the whole run of pieces is sent round the other way

explanation.definitionFit: A drink taken just before bed is a classic late evening beverage.

clue.text: Very occasionally artist is given backing by bank

indicators.note: the artist is backed by, i.e. followed by, the bank

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, a crossword artist
to bank on is to rely on

clue.text: Faithful servant given reduced rent

definitions.meaning: a lower fee paid to keep accommodation while away

clue.text: Parts of this Midlands area are, by implication, fantastic

definitions.text: Parts of this Midlands area are, by implication, fantastic

parts.words: Parts of this Midlands area are, by implication, fantastic
parts.note: the place-name splits into S, the word and, and W plus ELL

explanation.surface: A local boast that a Midlands district is wonderful.

explanation.definitionFit: A metropolitan borough near Birmingham, so an area of the English Midlands.

clue.text: Foreign girl employed by busy vet temporarily

indicators.note: employed by means the name is working within the next words
